speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we start our journey for the next 50 years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our first 50 years tell an extraordinary story of diverse people overcoming great odds together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every move – whether it was a Government policy, a company's investment or a household's family decision – was uncharted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through sheer grit, our Pioneers braved the odds, brought up families and built a home and a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On 13 December 1965, Mr Lim Kim San presented the first Budget of the independent Republic of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The major concerns then were: Konfrontasi, the Communist threat and the Vietnam War.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Few in the world paid attention to little Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Against this backdrop, our Pioneers debated how to make a living, by making our place in this region and in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In that first Budget, Mr Lim said: "Whilst Independence has… given us greater freedom of action… we also acquire new responsibilities and new dimensions are added to our problems." Our Pioneers took on these new responsibilities and new dimensions seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, made the rousing call that we must never fear; one day, we would be a modern metropolis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Year by year, we made progress and successive generations built on what was achieved.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we had much to celebrate in SG50.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we are in a much better position than our Pioneers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we also face new responsibilities, new challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 1965, we raced to teach "123s" and "ABCs" to our young, and to create factory jobs to soak up unemployment for a young population.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, over 95% of our students progress beyond secondary school.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our challenge now is to take education beyond schools, to lifelong learning, and to grow the economy to create quality jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 1965, we were fighting childhood mortality with mass immunisation and distributing milk to under-nourished children.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our challenge is to find new ways to care for our elderly, to manage chronic diseases and to tackle childhood obesity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 1965, we were faced with Konfrontasi and the Vietnam War, and were at risk of social discord stemming from a legacy of racial conflict and pro-communism.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we have to guard ourselves against a more complex and diverse array of threats, from conventional threats to terrorism and cyber warfare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Lim Kim San's words 50 years ago resonate to this day.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We face a new world that brings its own freedoms and responsibilities, its own challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our mission remains unchanged – it is to find the ways to create opportunities for Singaporeans to grow and defend our home and our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taking inspiration from our Pioneers, we must plan ahead, stay united, be creative and build our future together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the context in which President Tony Tan set out five key aims for this term of Government: (a) renewing our economy; (b) fostering a more caring society; (c) transforming our urban landscape; (d) keeping Singapore safe and secure; (e) engaging and partnering Singaporeans in nation-building.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To achieve these goals, we must grow our economy and invest collectively for the long term – in our people, our home, our security.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To grow our economy, we will invest in building stronger enterprises and nurturing innovative industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our people, we will invest in education and health.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue investing in our people through education and SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our security, we will also have to invest more in intelligence, operational capabilities, technology and systems to keep our home safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our expenditures have grown to almost two-and-a-half times what they were 10 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We were able to fund these increased investments because we had planned ahead and remained prudent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Growth had also been fairly strong, as our gross domestic product (GDP) almost doubled over the last decade.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this term, we are starting from a position of strength.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have anticipated our needs and made provisions in the last term.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have no natural resources, no oil wells, but we benefit significantly from the returns of the Reserves accumulated by our forefathers through hard work and thrift.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to strike a careful balance between what we spend today and what we save for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the longer term, to meet Singapore's many needs, especially in healthcare, our expenditures will grow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But GDP growth will slow as our economy and workforce mature.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will find ourselves in a tighter fiscal position.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must grow our capabilities in order to grow our economy and create good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must remain prudent in our expenditures and ensure every additional dollar spent is spent responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must encourage every Singaporean to contribute towards caring for our fellow citizens and building for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am confident that if we have the will, we will find the way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Core for us to succeed is the spirit of partnership, where Singaporeans work together in new ways to transform our economy and strengthen our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have inherited a strong spirit of togetherness from our kampung days.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, it has taken on new forms and new vitality, from the shared values of Our Singapore Conversation, to the ground-up active citizenry of SG50, to the collective commitment in "The Future of Us and SGfuture".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, this partnership that is at the heart of the Singapore spirit will become even more critical for tackling big challenges together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone has a role and, together, we are weaving a rich tapestry – each thread a different colour and texture, but woven together to give strength and resilience to our economy and our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must come together as partners to transform our economy through enterprise and deeper innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economy is becoming more interconnected, more diverse and complex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Change is accelerating, with rapid advances in knowledge and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet, the potential for collaboration has never been greater.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must work together to muster our resources, to innovate, scale up and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our economic transformation will draw on the strengths of individual schemes, businesses, unions and trade associations, but bring everyone together in a more tightly-woven tapestry to meet the specific needs of our industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Likewise, we must deepen partnerships to build a caring and resilient society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the last decade, the Government has stepped up social support significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we must continue to build both individual and collective responsibility, for it is together that they make for a stronger society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our next phase, we will strengthen partnerships with community groups to build a rich tapestry of caring communities in all our neighbourhoods, with multiple layers of support, drawing on different threads of care and kindness, but integrated coherently.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Leading up to this Budget, we received thousands of suggestions and feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me thank all who have contributed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2016 is the beginning of a journey towards SG100.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the spirit of partnership, we will transform our economy through enterprise and innovation and build a caring and resilient society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Productivity growth has not been as strong as we would like.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The performance across sectors was varied: wholesale and retail trade, and finance and insurance did well, while manufacturing – in particular, the marine and offshore segment – declined, as can be seen in the chart above.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am aware that current business conditions are difficult and uncertain.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of our firms are facing weaker top-line growth, rising manpower costs and tighter financing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Workers are anxious as retrenchment has increased, including among professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the coming year, given our economy's heavy dependence on external demand, the weaknesses in the global economy will pose strong headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pace of global economic recovery is uneven, with the United States (US) being the most advanced, while Europe and Japan will only see modest growth aided by monetary stimulus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Closer to home, China is going through a transition towards a more sustainable growth path.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a complex transition and any short-term setbacks may create volatility in the financial markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We, therefore, expect externally-oriented sectors such as manufacturing to continue to face subdued demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The extended downturn in oil and other commodity prices is affecting commodity-related activities, particularly the marine and offshore sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Weak global demand in electronics will spill over to related sectors, such as precision engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But while overall growth is subdued, our business landscape is varied.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even within manufacturing, the medtech and chemicals segments are growing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Exports of services, including tourism, financial services, information and communications technology (ICT) and consultancy, are benefiting from regional demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Domestic-oriented sectors, such as retail, healthcare and education, have been, and should remain, stable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Construction, too, will be supported by a large expansion in public infrastructure and housing projects, even as private residential demand has ebbed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some are becoming more competitive and gaining market share, while others are seeking to relocate to cheaper locations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Similarly, prospects in the labour market are mixed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, redundancies increased in 2015 as global demand slowed and restructuring continued.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of those made redundant took longer to find jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While some sectors, such as the offshore and marine and manufacturing, are retrenching staff, others, such as healthcare, education and ICT, are hiring.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, while conditions are difficult, we should not be overly pessimistic.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we tackle immediate cyclical weaknesses, we must be alert to major structural changes abroad and at home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Major economies are continuing to restructure and will alter the global competitive landscape in the process.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: China is rebalancing towards consumption and services-led growth and developing innovation-intensive industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: India is building on its strengths in ICT and seeking to attract manufacturing investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These ongoing changes are rapidly changing the patterns of trade and specialisation in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technological changes, especially in robotics, automation, artificial intelligence and ICT, are disrupting business models across all sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some call the coming changes "Industrial Revolution 4.0." At home, manpower growth is slowing and our population is ageing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Real wage increases over the past few years have benefited workers and households.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But unless productivity improves in tandem, we will be less competitive and both businesses and workers will be worse off.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these changes pose intense challenges for our businesses, which will have to succeed in a more competitive environment while contending with tighter labour constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The need to restructure is both urgent and critical.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The ASEAN Economic Community, the Trans-Pacific Partnership and China's One Belt One Road initiative will open up new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are well-placed to benefit from technological changes – our investments in education, R&D and digital infrastructure will enable us to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also started restructuring early and our firms, including SMEs, are embarking on change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people are valued for their integrity, adaptability and their multi-cultural sensitivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is regarded as a highly-connected, trusted node.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In summary, we face near-term cyclical weaknesses, which affect various sectors in different degrees, as well as medium-term structural challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we are well-positioned to manage these challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2016 has three key thrusts to address the challenges in our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, to address cyclical weaknesses, we will adopt an expansionary fiscal stance to provide some counter.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, together with relief measures targeted at SMEs, will provide support in the near term.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The aim is to enable our firms to emerge stronger to benefit from the broader global recovery when it takes place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will support our people through change, by enabling them to learn new skills, especially in new, fast-growing sectors, and in facilitating employment and job-matching.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To tackle medium- to long-term issues, we have convened the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Though CFE has just begun work, the inputs have been valuable for the measures in this Budget and, as the deliberations continue, we will update our plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first source of support for firms comes from existing measures and public spending, including public infrastructure projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, total spending is expected to be $5 billion, or 7.3% higher than in FY2015.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The increases are mainly in healthcare, education, security and urban development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Transition Support Package that was introduced in financial year (FY) 2013 will also continue to support our firms in raising productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, this month, firms will receive a total of $1.9 billion for qualifying wage increases given under the Wage Credit Scheme13, the largest payout to date.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, public sector demand for construction projects is expected to increase significantly in 2016, helping to mitigate a decline in private sector construction demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes more than $2.5 billion of public sector contracts for smaller projects14, which will benefit smaller construction firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The last time we had a 50% rebate was in YA 200115.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The higher percentage rebate is targeted at SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The increased support is expected to cost an additional $180 million over two years, bringing the total support to companies under the CIT rebate to close to $1 billion over two years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in addition to the wage offset of 3% for the re-employment of workers aged 65 and above till the re-employment age is raised in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under this scheme, the Government will co-share 50% of the default risk of such loans with participating financial institutions to encourage lending to our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SME Working Capital Loan will be available for three years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This could catalyse more than $2 billion of loans over this period.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fifth, we will help our heartland shops to be more vibrant, as these shops give our neighbourhoods a sense of community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) will enhance the Revitalisation of Shops package to better support promotional activities and upgrading projects in the Housing and Development Board (HDB) town centres and neighbourhood centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) will also work with the Federation of Merchants' Associations and local merchant associations to strengthen their capabilities to support heartland businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This enhanced initiative is expected to cost about $15 million annually.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Manufacturing Work Permit levies will remain unchanged for another year, as announced at Budget 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will proceed with levy increases for Services and Construction Work Permit holders, as well as S Pass holders in every sector, as announced in Budget 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in view of the fact that the foreign workforce has continued to grow in these areas over the past year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, this calibrated set of measures is appropriate to address the near-term concerns of our firms, especially SMEs, while enabling restructuring.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have asked for a repeat of the support measures we saw in 2009.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But that was when the economy was already in deep recession and facing huge uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For now, while the outlook is soft, MTI expects positive growth in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must not let pessimism take hold, lest it creates self-fulfilling expectations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the situation and it stands ready to act if conditions warrant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have also asked about the range of measures that we have introduced to stabilise the property market since 2010.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are intended to keep the market stable and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Based on the price level and current market conditions, our assessment is that it is premature to relax these measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to monitor developments in the property market closely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we provide immediate relief and support amid the current cyclical slowdown, we must press on with economic transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economic landscape is changing and our challenges are pressing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must find every opportunity to transform, to emerge stronger in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Budget 2016, we will launch a new Industry Transformation Programme to take us into the next phase of our development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This builds on our efforts under the Quality Growth Programme, which was introduced in Budget 2013 to achieve inclusive growth driven by innovation and higher productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Industry Transformation Programme will help firms and industries to create new value and drive growth in four ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, it will involve integrating our different restructuring efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our efforts to raise productivity, develop our people and drive research and innovation are working, but we can maximise the impact by pulling these together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will take a more targeted and sector-focused approach to better meet the needs of firms in each sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will deepen partnerships among the Government, workers and the industry, and among industry players to identify challenges and develop solutions to support transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And fourth, we will place a stronger emphasis on technology adoption and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Food Manufacturing sector is a good example of how such an approach can work.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Individually, our Singapore food companies have put in place many innovations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some, such as Tan Seng Kee, have used technology to develop a whole range of products which stay fresh for longer.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This enabled Tan Seng Kee to be the first company in Singapore to export fresh noodles that can be easily prepared with its special sauce mixes in flavours, such as laksa and curry mee.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others, such as Foodgnostic, have transformed their business models to enhance business growth through internationalisation and food exports.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an industry, our food manufacturers built on their innovations and Singapore's trusted reputation for high quality and safe food to jointly create the "Tasty Singapore" brand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Using this brand, they are internationalising and selling to China, India, the Middle East and even Africa.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are now expanding through e-commerce, using websites, such as Tmall.com.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The combined novelty and quality of their individual products allowed them to stand out as a group.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The sharing of common facilities gave them economies of scale.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And building the Singapore brand together won them global recognition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In turn, their success creates a virtuous cycle of investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our food industry has also been investing in their people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include 280 management associates and interns they see as future leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There have been strong partnerships across firms, as well as among firms and the Singapore Food Manufacturing Association (SFMA), the Food Innovation Resource Centre in Singapore Polytechnic17 and various Government agencies18.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a result, what once appeared to be a sunset industry – because of low margins and high labour cost – is now a thriving sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Value-add per worker has grown considerably from 2010 to 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Food Manufacturing sector shows the importance of mindset.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As one of the industry's leaders told me: "There is no such thing as a sunset industry, only sunset thinking!" It shows that transformation comes not only from individual firms but the industry as a whole working together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will set out three key thrusts under the Industry Transformation Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will support the transformation of enterprises, to build deep capabilities, deploy technology, develop scale and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will support the transformation of industries at the industry level, to adopt technology and innovate faster, come up with common industry solutions to common problems, seek new markets overseas and deepen industry partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprises are the building blocks of our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Vibrant enterprises that change and transform with the times create growth and buzz in the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Take the example of Xin Ming Hua Private Limited.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Started as a small machinery and repair shop in 1955, it is now one of the largest distributors of engines and power systems in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been active in innovating and building up in-house design and manufacturing capabilities; adopting automation to achieve productivity gains of up to 75% with the help of Republic Polytechnic19; and internationalising and scaling up its operations to serve customers better.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support many more firms to transform successfully, we will introduce several measures in this Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we have a wide range of schemes administered by various Government agencies to help enterprises20 of different sizes across industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help SMEs access these schemes, we established SME Centres and stepped up our outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Still, many firms found the range of incentive schemes and agencies confusing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, it is an alphabet soup, as shown on this slide: it is scheme-centric, not enterprise-centric.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This portal will be organised along the core business needs of capability building, training and international expansion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms will not need to go from agency to agency to figure out which schemes apply to them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The portal will also pre-populate details that are available in the ACRA database.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Business Grants Portal will start with grants from IE Singapore, SPRING, Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and Design Singapore and progressively include grants from other Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also continue to review and simplify the various support schemes to improve access and strengthen assistance for enterprises at various stages of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Currently, there is no support for the scaling up of automation projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As these involve significant financial outlays, some companies find it difficult to commit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The new Automation Support Package from SPRING will comprise four components.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will improve SMEs' access to loans for qualifying projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fourth, as such large-scale automation projects enable firms to scale and internationalise, IE Singapore will work closely together with SPRING in relevant cases to help these businesses to access overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third set of measures to transform enterprises is to support scaling up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will expand the SME Mezzanine Growth Fund from the current fund size of $100 million to a total fund size of up to $150 million.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will do so by matching up to $25 million of new private sector investment on a one-to-one basis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will provide more capital to support our SMEs to scale up and internationalise21.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support more mergers and acquisitions (M&As), I will grant the M&A allowance of up to $40 million of the value of the deal, instead of the current cap of $20 million.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details on these tax incentives can be found in the Annex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our firms, especially SMEs, are eager to seek new markets and new growth opportunities overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the coming years, IE Singapore will support more firms in their internationalisation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2016, IE expects to help around 35,000 to 40,000 companies of all sizes to venture overseas22.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This covers qualifying expenses incurred for activities, such as participation in overseas business development and investment study trips.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have outlined the four sets of measures to help individual enterprises transform.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will find it easier to transform if their entire industry also undertakes transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By doing it together, firms achieve scale, drive down cost, incentivise service providers to step forward and expand mindshare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second thrust of our Industry Transformation Programme is thus to support industry-level transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, robots can handle metal fabrication processes more efficiently, from steel cutting to welding to machine tending.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But these may be too expensive or complicated for many SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Recently, a number of solution providers, including Lincoln Electric, came forward to design and deliver more affordable, modular systems for SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over 1,000 SMEs could benefit, if this is scaled up across the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industry-level transformation works best if firms partner one another, or if industry associations lead the effort, because they know their needs best.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Government agencies can support by initialising lead demand or through regulatory changes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to form close partnerships among firms, industry associations and the Government to drive industry-level transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will develop a National Trade Platform (NTP) as the next-generation platform to support firms, particularly in the logistics and trade finance sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will eventually replace our current TradeNet and TradeXchange systems.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a one-stop trade information management system, the NTP will enable electronic data sharing among businesses and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms only have to provide trade information once and authorise its use by logistics providers as well as business partners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The information can also be used for Customs and other trade regulatory approvals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be especially helpful for SMEs to cut costs and streamline processes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will develop it as an open innovation platform, so that other service providers can develop value-added services and apps in areas, such as operations, visibility and trade finance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has the potential to bring over $600 million worth of man-hour savings each year for our firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A second way to drive industry-level transformation is to develop and deploy new technologies to solve problems that are relevant for the entire industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Robotics technology can enable us to work more effectively in a tight labour market.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It can also create more high value-added jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our hospitals, robotic technology is used in the pharmacy to pick medication accurately and quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This frees up time for pharmacy staff to provide advice on medication.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Autonomous transporters are used to move supplies efficiently in the hospital.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our hospitals are also trying power-assisted bed transport technologies to reduce the manual effort in moving patients.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these technologies can improve efficiency and transform the healthcare industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from healthcare, robotics and automation technology can be applied widely to transform sectors, such as Construction, Manufacturing and Logistics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We announced the National Robotics Programme last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third way to drive industry-level transformation is through our trade associations and chambers (TACs).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: TACs have intimate knowledge of the needs and potential of their specific sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are well-placed to reach out to many firms, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build on the existing Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) programme to help our TACs strengthen their outreach through the new LEAD-Plus programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will provide wider funding support for TACs to attract talent, develop their capabilities and strengthen their processes and services.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To forge a closer partnership and enable public officers to better understand the needs of our firms, we will also second up to 20 public officers to interested TACs as part of the LEAD-Plus programme over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, TACs can support firms to build capabilities and lead the development of industry-wide solutions for common challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have already expressed interest and SPRING will announce these soon.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I just spoke about how we can drive transformation at the industry-level by leveraging platform solutions and new technologies and increasing industry outreach through TACs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This builds on enterprise-level transformation and strengthens our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Innovation is critical to the Industry Transformation Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of the successful enterprise and industry-level transformations I described earlier have some elements of innovation in the form of new products or services, new processes, or new business or organisation models.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Innovation is enabled and enhanced by the use of technology, but innovation goes beyond that.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is fundamentally about new ways of doing things to meet the needs of people and industries better.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Innovation is the engine of value creation and growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must make innovation pervasive in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a long-term endeavour but let me outline some steps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will continue to deepen industry capabilities in innovation and research and development (R&D).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This represents a concerted shift towards innovation and enterprise, to capture the economic and social value of R&D.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Procter and Gamble (P&G) has worked with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) and Economic Development Board (EDB) to set up the Singapore Innovation Centre (SgIC).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is one of P&G's major innovation centres, focusing on research and product development for its global business units in Home Care, Healthcare, Grooming and Skin Care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SgIC will be a key open innovation hub to accelerate and facilitate collaborations between P&G and partners in Asia, including Singapore enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The ownership of intellectual property (IP) allows companies to realise the value of its efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A second way to transform through innovation is to promote startups in new and existing industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been nurturing our startup ecosystem, including venture funding and support for accelerators and incubators25.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The startup scene today is more vibrant, with growing funding support from venture and private equity funds.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SG-Innovate will match budding entrepreneurs with mentors, introduce them to venture capital firms, help them to access talent in research institutes and open up new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SG-Innovate will build on what has been done by the Infocomm Investments Private Limited (IIPL), and work with SPRING and EDB to expand the accelerator programmes to new and emerging sectors, such as Smart Energy, Digital Manufacturing, Fintech, Digital Health and Internet-of-Things.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A third way to transform through innovation is to create an open and innovative urban environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will launch an exciting new development: the Jurong Innovation District.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will be the future of innovation for enterprise, learning and living.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fifty years ago, we transformed Jurong from swampland into a thriving hub for the manufacturing industry that powered Singapore's economic growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will now make another leap to create the industrial park of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our earlier industrial estates were developed for specific industries, focused mostly on production.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, however, learning, research, innovation and production are closely intertwined.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Jurong Innovation District will create an environment to house these different activities within a single, next-generation industrial district.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has the potential to transform how we live, work, play, learn and create.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jurong Town Corporation (JTC) is currently constructing Launchpad @ JID, to serve as a space for entrepreneurs, researchers and students to design, prototype and test-bed their new innovations26.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: JTC has also launched an Open Innovation Call to invite private sector technology owners to test-bed and develop innovative and sustainable infrastructure solutions within the District.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In parallel, we will be building JID progressively, with the first phase targeted for completion around 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Similarly, we are investing in infrastructure for the future, such as Changi Airport Terminal 5, to better connect us to the world and to test innovative solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, I will make a further $1 billion top-up to the Changi Airport Development Fund to support this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are launching the Industry Transformation Programme to transform our enterprises, transform industries and transform through innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These three thrusts will take concerted partnership to realise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have highlighted a few examples of how enterprises and entire industries can embark on this transformation journey, but these are just a beginning.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a Government, we must adopt a more integrated approach to support transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our agencies will work more closely together, integrating their different support schemes to take a more targeted approach to developing each industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work closely with enterprises and, at the industry-level, to develop transformation maps for each sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will help us allocate the resources to develop each sector appropriately.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the next tranche of increased funding to SPRING, IE Singapore and EDB to support economic development, as well as new resources for measures announced in this Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These resources will support the sectors under the Industry Transformation Programme, as well as to cater for the growth of new industries over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The actual spending will depend on the take-up rates of the various schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The work with sectors, such as precision engineering and logistics, is at a more advanced stage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These maps will be "live" documents that we have to adjust as we navigate our way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We may not have all the answers today, but we must work together – our people, firms, unions and Government agencies – in a spirit of partnership and to keep experimenting and trying, in the spirit of enterprise and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we move towards more targeted measures under the Industry Transformation Programme, I will continue the tapering of broad-based measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: PIC, currently, has two components: cash payout and tax deductions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The 400% tax deductions under the scheme remain unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even with the tapering of these broad-based measures, we will continue to provide significant support for firms to restructure in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The details of these changes are in the Annex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget sets the direction, taking into account feedback from businesses during the initial phase of the work of CFE.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As CFE deliberates and consults more widely, we will adjust, but we must start to move in the new direction early.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As firms face weaknesses in cyclical demand and structural challenges, our people, too, will be directly affected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Singaporeans have been retrenched, while others are anxious about their future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even where new jobs are being created, they wonder if they can keep up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, as economic cycles shorten and changes occur faster, the pressure on our people to adapt will rise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: People all over the world are facing this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I understand Singaporeans' anxieties and concerns and we must give every support to our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One major way is for our firms to restructure, so that our workers have better prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This chart shows that across selected industries28, firms with higher productivity tend to pay higher wages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is important for our firms to raise productivity, or else our workers would remain in low value-added jobs with weak prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must aim for a virtuous cycle of higher skills, higher productivity and higher wages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Industry Transformation Programme I outlined earlier will be a major effort to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even in new sectors that are growing, such as ICT, new skills are constantly needed as technologies change rapidly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, with the exponential growth of social and mobile offerings by businesses, employers are looking for software engineers with skills in User Interface and Design, Android/iOS development, Application Programming Interfaces on top of the commonly used programming languages like Python, C++ and Java.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, like firms, our people, too, are facing cyclical and structural changes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I appreciate that it is not easy for those who are retrenched to learn new skills and find new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if we remain adaptable, learn, unlearn and relearn quickly, we can stay relevant and seek new careers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the robust attitude of Singaporeans towards changes, and our willingness to learn, we are better-placed than many others elsewhere to cope with change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people are increasingly better-educated and we are investing significantly in life-long learning and skills development under SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our polytechnics and universities have responded to the changing job market.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, our polytechnics now offer new courses, such as cybersecurity and digital forensics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) also now trains food technologists29.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dealing with change will be a long-term endeavour and for this Budget, the Government will, together with employers and unions, support our people in three ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, through SkillsFuture, we will support our people to keep learning new skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will help those who have been laid off to find new work and build a new career.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will pilot new approaches to job matching and training, to enable more people to seize new opportunities in growth sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since we launched SkillsFuture in November 2014, we have put in place many initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will enable our people to identify and pursue their interests at every stage of life and to broaden and deepen their skills with better education and training.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we have announced SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programmes in 12 sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since January, Singaporeans have also started using the SkillsFuture Credit to learn new skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SkillsFuture Study Awards, which support individuals to develop specialist skills, is taking off nicely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since October last year, the response has been good and we have rolled out the study awards covering 12 areas of specialisation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Take, for example, Ms Yap Chui Hoon, who will be using the SkillsFuture Study Award to deepen her skills as a social worker.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After graduating with an ITE certificate, she worked for more than 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She learnt on the job with the help of multiple part-time courses, including diplomas in social service and disability studies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are off to a good start and must continue to expand and deepen SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help our people adapt to changing job demands and grow their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For workers who may face greater difficulty in finding jobs, we will expand our wage support schemes to encourage firms to hire them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will benefit more workers who may be affected by retrenchments or business restructuring.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For mid-career jobseekers, including retrenched professionals, we will step up professional conversion programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New programmes will be launched in sectors, such as Design and ICT.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The final thrust of our efforts is to support our people to acquire new skills and match them to new opportunities in growing sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The demand for ICT professionals is growing because it can enable many new businesses as well as disrupt existing ones.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To drive our Smart Nation effort, we will need many more of our own experts, in a wide variety of skills – programmers and coders, cybersecurity specialists, user experience designers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Major IT employers and associations, including the Singapore infocomm Technology Federation (SiTF), Singapore Computer Society (SCS) and IT Management Association (ITMA), will partner IDA in this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: TechSkills Accelerator will pioneer a new way of enabling our people to acquire expertise and skills, so as to engage in the fast-growing ICT sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will: (a) identify specific skills in demand and work with specialised training providers to meet these complex demands in startups and in sectors, such as finance and healthcare; (b) develop industry-recognised skills standards and certification.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will guide ICT professionals to acquire industry-relevant skills and help employers assess the skills proficiency of their employees; (c) work with anchor employers to commit to hiring and paying based on certified skills proficiency rather than academic qualifications alone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several employers have agreed to come on board, including the Government Technology Agency.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: TechSkills Accelerator will pioneer new ways of enabling Singaporeans to be at the frontiers of learning and knowledge to seize opportunities in new growth areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand these efforts to more sectors in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As announced at Budget 2015, we estimate that our spending on SkillsFuture and related initiatives will average over $1 billion per year till 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministers for Communications and Information, Education, Manpower, National Development and Trade and Industry will elaborate on the various measures that I have spoken about at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through all these measures, Budget 2016 seeks a new way to transform our economy through enterprise and innovation, with stronger partnerships among stakeholders to support our people to manage change.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have spent some time on how we will transform our economy through enterprise and innovation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We seek to transform our economy so that we continue to have the resources and opportunities for our home to be safe, and for our people to find fulfilment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together with a strong economy, we need to build a caring and resilient society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We want a Singapore which is a great place to raise a family and where we bring out the best in every Singaporean; a society that takes care of those who have special needs, who are less well-off or who have fallen on hard times; a society where our seniors age with energy and dignity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the last decade, the Government has invested more in our schools and preschools.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have done more for families with children, through measures like the Baby Bonus and additional leave for parents.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have strengthened the four pillars of our social security system: home ownership, healthcare assurance, Central Provident Fund (CPF) and Workfare.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have also enhanced ComCare and made help more accessible through the Social Service Offices.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget builds on what we have done and looks at new ways to build a caring and resilient society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will forge a deeper partnership among individuals, the community and the Government, catalyse ground-up initiatives to build caring and cohesive neighbourhoods and pilot new ways to reach out to our seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will apply to eligible babies born from today.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am told that, on average last year, we had 93 babies born every day.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, congratulations to the 93 babies born today.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Parents who save more will continue to receive dollar-for-dollar matching from the Government, up to the co-savings cap.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For example, if they put $3,000 into their first or second child's CDA, they will receive an additional $3,000 in matching grants, bringing the total Government CDA grant to $6,000, for a total of $9,000 in the account.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Similarly, parents with more children will receive the CDA First Step grant.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Details are in the Annex   The Senior Minister of State in charge of the National Population and Talent Division will elaborate on further measures to make Singapore a great place for families at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Next, we will pilot a new initiative, called KidSTART, for children in their first six years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There is extensive research which shows that experiences in the early years of a child's life significantly influence his or her physical, cognitive and social development.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have been enhancing development programmes through our pre-schools and primary schools.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: However, there is a small group of parents who may need more support to give their children a good start in life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: KidSTART will draw together Government and community resources, to help these children receive appropriate learning, developmental and health support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will elaborate on this at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also do more to help families with children in rental housing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Prime Minister mentioned the Fresh Start Housing Scheme at last year's National Day Rally.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are some families who previously bought a flat, but sold it, and are now living in public rental flats.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These families are not eligible for housing grants for first-timers, as they had received a housing subsidy before.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For those who are determined to work hard to own a home again, we want to give them a fresh start.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Families will need to demonstrate effort, for example, by staying employed and making sure their children attend school.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for National Development will provide more details at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To thrive, our young people need a sense of adventure, resilience and be ready to challenge themselves to be their best.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help our students develop these attributes, we will expand outdoor adventure education for all students, through a new National Outdoor Adventure Education Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As part of this effort, we will build a new Outward Bound Singapore (OBS) campus on Coney Island.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many more youths will have the chance to go for an expedition with OBS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These activities will help them build confidence and develop camaraderie with students across different schools.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Just like the OBS campus on Pulau Ubin, it will be rustic and blend in with the rest of the island.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Coney Island remains open for everyone to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and Ministry of Education (MOE) will provide more details later.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For our children and youths, we concentrate on providing them opportunities through education.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For adults, we focus on opportunities through work – through which we learn and contribute and derive personal pride and dignity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are three groups who may need more support in the workforce: seniors, low-wage workers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We can do more together to help them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I spoke earlier about the extension of the SEC, to encourage employers to hire seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will now speak about helping our low-wage workers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme has encouraged workers who are 35 years old and above to join the workforce, by supplementing their income and CPF savings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: WIS will continue to help the bottom 20% of workers, with some support also provided to those in the 30th income percentile.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Payouts will vary, depending on their age and income.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Workers will continue to receive 40% of WIS in cash and 60% in CPF.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To illustrate, an older worker aged 55 earning $1,200 a month will now get a total of $2,900 a year from WIS, with about $1,200 in cash and $1,700 in CPF a year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: He will then have $3,500 more in his CPF account at age 65.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also simplify the qualifying criteria for WIS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, to receive WIS, one has to work two out of three consecutive months, or three out of six consecutive months, or six out of 12 months in a year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will now pay WIS for every month worked.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: By simplifying the qualifying criteria, workers can also look forward to receiving WIS payments more quickly – monthly rather than quarterly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many persons with disabilities also want the opportunity to contribute through work.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, those who meet the WIS eligibility criteria receive WIS, even if they are under 35 years old.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They will benefit from the WIS enhancements I spoke about earlier.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Employers who hire persons with disabilities who earn up to $4,000 a month will continue to receive the SEC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They get a credit of up to 16% of the employee's wages, twice as large as the SEC for older workers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Currently, only low-wage workers 35 years old and above are eligible for the Workfare Training Support scheme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will now also enable persons with disabilities who earn low wages and are under 35 years old, to be eligible for the Workfare Training Support scheme, so that we can better support them in their learning.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Public Service will play its part in expanding job opportunities for persons with disabilities, with support from SGEnable.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will speak on the review of the national Enabling Masterplan at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There will be many more seniors amongst us in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The proportion of Singaporeans aged 65 and above will double from one in eight today, to one in four by 2030.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: How we adjust and turn this into a source of strength will shape our society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together, we must, and will make Singapore a model for successful ageing and empower all to age with dignity and vitality.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In this Budget, we will increase retirement support for seniors who have lesser means.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also build strong communities, to support active ageing and engagement in the community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At Budget 2015, we spoke about the introduction of the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is a major new feature in our social security system.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some of our older Singaporeans have fewer resources in their retirement years than others, because they earned low wages even after working consistently throughout their lives, or because they stayed home to raise their families.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The aim of Silver Support is to support the bottom 20% of Singaporeans aged 65 and above, with a smaller degree of support extended to cover up to 30% of seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It can be a modest but meaningful supplement to their retirement incomes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is not intended to substitute other sources of support, whether from their own savings or family support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Silver Support also complements other forms of assistance they may receive from existing schemes, whether it is Workfare, healthcare subsidies or the Goods and Services (GST) Voucher.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Silver Support is not only for the neediest of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For the truly needy, we have the safety net of Public Assistance (PA), which I will speak about shortly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the past year or so, we have deliberated with care on the fairest way of identifying those who are the bottom 20% to 30% of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As no single criterion allows us to assess needs and operationalise the scheme effectively, we will use three criteria in combination – lifetime wages, housing type and the level of household support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The first criterion, lifetime wages, is measured by the amount the individual has contributed into his CPF accounts in total30 by the age of 55.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We do not look at CPF contributions after 55, to encourage older Singaporeans to continue working.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Silver Support will cover the seniors who live in and own a 4-room or smaller HDB flat31.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Seniors who live in 5-room HDB flats, but do not own the flat, will also qualify if they meet the other criteria.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together, these three criteria allow us to make sure Silver Support goes to those who have lower incomes over their lifetimes and less retirement support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: About half of the seniors living in 3-room flats will also receive Silver Support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To illustrate, take a retired couple living in a 3-room flat.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each had put less than $70,000 into their CPF accounts by the age of 55, perhaps because they were in low-wage jobs throughout their working lives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: By all three counts, the couple qualify for Silver Support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will not change or stop any other support they are receiving, such as the GST Voucher or healthcare subsidies through CHAS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For such couples, Silver Support can be very meaningful.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There may also be some seniors in lower-income households who qualify for Silver Support, but subsequently no longer need it, for example, because their children are able to provide stronger financial support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The converse may also happen, resulting in the senior needing more support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, we will make an assessment annually to take into account changes in circumstances, to make sure we target Silver Support at those with lesser means.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We earlier announced that we would implement Silver Support around the first quarter of 2016.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The next two payouts will be made in end-September and end-December.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each one is a payout for the coming quarter.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In subsequent years, payouts will be made in March, June, September and December.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: CPF Board will notify eligible seniors before the first payout is made.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There is no need for seniors to apply; this will happen automatically.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The cost will likely increase over time as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The majority of our seniors, even if they do not qualify for Silver Support, will continue to benefit from substantial existing support schemes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These include the GST Voucher, higher healthcare subsidies through MediShield Life premium subsidies and the Pioneer Generation Package, foreign domestic worker levy concessions, and ElderCare subsidies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some could also choose to realise the value of the property they own, through renting it out, or making use of the enhanced Lease Buyback Scheme or the Silver Housing Bonus.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is on top of the support from children which many receive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We care about enabling our seniors to stay active and healthy, to stay meaningfully engaged.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I recently met Mrs Lucy Tan, who is the Cluster Director of PEACE-Connect.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: PEACE-Connect has been taking care of needy seniors in Kampong Glam for the last 20 years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Lucy related to me how she has seen the social and medical needs of the seniors evolve over the years – they grew ever more complex, affecting more and more seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Lucy and her organisation had to evolve, too.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She realised PEACE-Connect would have to work with more partners if they wanted to support seniors better.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She has been developing partnerships with other organisations and, with the support of her Advisor, Ms Denise Phua, she has integrated these resources well.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For instance, she works with Kampong Glam CC to provide subsidised meals daily to some residents in the area, and links seniors up with services that they need at Town Councils and Social Service Offices.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Lucy shows what is possible when we strengthen partnerships.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These networks will comprise local stakeholders, such as voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), community volunteers, schools and businesses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the core, the network will have a small team of full-time officers who will study the health and social needs of seniors and draw together stakeholders to provide coordinated support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We hope to help seniors discover health conditions earlier and manage them well, while connecting those who are healthy and mobile to a wide range of activities to encourage seniors to stay active, healthy and engaged in the community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Under this pilot, our Pioneer Generation Ambassadors will, through their outreach, encourage seniors to stay active and connect them to relevant support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There will be a group of seniors who may require more help, such as frail elderly living alone, who have limited family support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These networks will provide more targeted and coordinated health and social support for them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: By integrating the resources and efforts of Government agencies, VWOs and local volunteers, these networks can make a big difference to support seniors to stay active and engaged.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It will also be a new way of service delivery and a meaningful way to realise the Action Plan for Successful Ageing launched last year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will pilot these Community Networks for Seniors in a few areas.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
