text: If successful, this pilot can be scaled up later.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have spoken about our care measures for the young, low-wage workers and those with disabilities and seniors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also provide additional support to households in general.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Those who are permanently unable to work and have little or no means of income and family support, currently receive free or highly-subsidised social services and free medical treatment in polyclinics and public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In addition, they receive a basic monthly cash allowance through the Public Assistance scheme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Additional amounts are provided for families with children, and for needs, such as medical supplies and household appliances.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will announce more details at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To support households amid current economic conditions, we will provide a one-off GST Voucher – Cash Special Payment of up to $200 for eligible GST Voucher – Cash recipients.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In total, eligible households can receive up to $500 in GSTV – Cash in 2016   If our recipients spend some of these in our neighbourhood shops, it will support our local businesses as well!

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We currently have 15 personal income tax reliefs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have enhanced many of these over the years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each tax relief serves a worthy objective, such as to supplement retirement savings, encourage mothers to work after having children, or take up a course.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At this threshold, 99% of tax-resident individuals will not be affected.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For instance, among those currently claiming the Working Mother's Child Relief, nine out of 10 are expected to continue to claim it fully, without being affected by this cap.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This cap will make our personal income tax system more progressive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Nevertheless, our personal income tax burden remains low.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our personal income tax structure must allow us to continue to stay competitive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The personal income tax relief cap will take effect from YA 2018 and is expected to raise an additional $100 million a year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, our schools have meaningful values-in-action programmes for our students to help others.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At work, businesses are well-placed to run impactful programmes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We should give a boost to Corporate Social Responsibility and make it easier for employees to contribute through their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget will support the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre's efforts to promote and build capacity for giving among corporates.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For instance, Samsui Supplies and Service, a food retailer, uses their kitchen facilities to prepare 2,000 free meals a day for the needy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must encourage more businesses to step forward.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Budget will also catalyse more ground-up initiatives, to better tap on the creativity and energy of Singaporeans, many of whom want to give back.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Such citizen-initiated efforts can drive community-based and neighbourhood-based initiatives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Currently, we allow for 250% tax deduction for donations of cash, and qualifying in-kind donations, such as land and computers, to certain Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This has seen good results, with cash donations rising each year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many employees also want to volunteer and we hope businesses will support them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To do so, I will introduce a Business and IPC Partnership Scheme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: From 1 July 2016 till the end of 2018, businesses that organise their employees to volunteer and provide services to IPCs, including secondments, will receive a 250% tax deduction on associated cost incurred, subject to the receiving IPC's agreement.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This deduction will be subject to a yearly cap of $250,000 per business and $50,000 per IPC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Community Chest (ComChest) plays a critical role in raising funds for about 80 VWOs across the entire social sector, including the Family Service Centres and special education schools.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: ComChest's monthly donation programme, SHARE, enables it to receive regular donations, through payroll deductions or GIRO.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some businesses have been active in supporting SHARE.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To give a boost to ComChest's good work, I will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for any additional donations through SHARE, over and above the FY2015 level.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will do this for three years, starting from April this year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Where businesses encourage their staff to donate regularly, we will allow part of the matching funds to be used by them to organise Corporate Social Responsibility activities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will elaborate at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For SG50, we started the SG50 Celebration Fund.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We had a very good response and supported close to 400 projects initiated by Singaporeans from different walks of life to celebrate our Jubilee year and to build a sense of community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These are Ms Seema and Ms Harsha Dadlani, two Singaporean sisters who are passionate about writing and helping children learn.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With support from the SG50 Celebration Fund, they wrote and published six children's books about Singapore, which were very well-received.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Also, I recently met Mr Dennis Quek and Mr Wilson Ang.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They organised a project to take 100 wheelchair users on a tour of Pulau Ubin, getting help from over 600 people to do so, including help from the Singapore Navy to ferry the participants on navy vessels.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When I met them recently, I asked them why they did what they did.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They told me they just wanted to share the parts of Singapore they love with fellow Singaporeans who may not be able to have the same experiences that they had.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When I told them that it was kind of them to do so, they said they got a lot more out of the project than they put into it – in terms of learning, new friendships, appreciation for what can be achieved when many parts, many people come together for a common cause.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They were amazed at how many people came forward to realise the power of partnership.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is Our Singapore Fund because it is about how we can all come together in partnership to share our strengths and loves, create something more and better together, to build our Singapore together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Fund will support projects that build the spirit of caring and resilience, nurture our can-do spirit and promote unity and our sense of being Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will elaborate at COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I hope that these three measures will catalyse efforts for a kinder and more caring society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The details of these measures are in the Annex.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is Ms Norashidah binte Mohd Yassin, who is 39 years old this year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Three years ago, she was staying in interim rental housing with her two young children, without family support or income.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With the support of her Member of Parliament, Dr Maliki Osman, who coordinated the help from a welfare organisation, PAVE, grassroots volunteers and various Government agencies, she gradually got back on her feet.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She first took on ironing of clothes for her neighbours, then baking, after getting a baking certificate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She later got a job as an administrative assistant and was soon promoted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, her children are well-adjusted and she is waiting for her flat.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Her story is inspiring not just because of her remarkable progress, but also because she is now reaching out to help others who are in the same situation that she used to be in, counselling them and teaching them baking skills.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is the spirit of the society that we are building.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is one where we rise above our circumstances to build a better life for ourselves and our children.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is a society that cares for those in need and where those who are helped do their part to help others.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is a society that we are all proud to be a part of.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is lower than the deficit of $6.7 billion or 1.7% of GDP we had budgeted a year ago.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As we spend more, we must also spend right: to both provide immediate relief to businesses and support longer-term economic transformation; to both provide targeted support to those in need and invest in developing our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The rise in expenditure in FY2016 is supported by increases in both Operating Revenue and higher Net Investment Returns (NIR) Contributions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are benefiting from an increase in Operating Revenue this year due to one-off factors which we do not expect to be sustained32.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As mentioned earlier, the longer-term picture will grow more challenging as we expect expenditure needs to grow faster than revenues.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even as we plan for rising expenditures, we must spend only when it is needed and where it best achieves our social and economic objectives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our budget position seeks to strike a balance between being prudent, given the continued rise in expenditures we expect in the years ahead and being accommodating to support enterprises in the current economic climate even as we continue our restructuring efforts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Should economic conditions turn, we stand ready to adjust and respond.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I started today by recalling the first Budget of the Independent Republic of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Eight days after that first Budget was presented, our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew said that we must keep Singapore here a thousand years from now.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And he said, "That is your job and mine." A thousand years from now.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singapore was only 135 days old when he said that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And, more importantly, an indomitable will: for it is your job and mine, he said, to make sure we survive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If Singapore is to have a future, we have to work hard at it – together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is poignant to recall these words one year and one day after Mr Lee's passing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: He attended almost every Budget Day since 1959.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each of us has only so many years on this earth to do our best for one another and for our country.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We can dream, plan and build for a thousand years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Budget 2016 is the first step of the next lap in what we hope will be a long, successful journey.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For our economy, we will tackle immediate pressures head-on.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Through targeted efforts and close partnerships, we must drive scale and create value.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will build resilience in workers, enterprises and industries so that they can weather changes and emerge stronger.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And we will build a caring and resilient society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will find new ways of encouraging people and companies to come forward to help the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will find new ways of collaboration and social innovation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Just like our Pioneers had no textbooks to show them how Singapore could thrive in its first 50 years, we have no instruction manual for our future.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What we have are our shared values, our common vision, a sense of duty and the conviction that we are one people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together, we must harness the creativity and energy of every one of us to transform our economy and strengthen our society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We cannot always know the future and we would not always have ready answers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But we must have the imagination to forge new paths, the courage to try new ways and the tenacity to persevere if we do not succeed on the first try.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As long as we stand by our values, keep faith with one another, think long term, dare to try and be open to change, we will move in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When the new Cabinet was sworn in last year, the Prime Minister said, "The Singapore Story belongs to all of us.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If we have faith that Singapore will endure and thrive, and put our heart and soul into building Singapore, then we will prevail and secure our place in history." That is your duty and mine.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Singapore Story belongs to all of us.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are many chapters yet to be written in that story.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Let us put our heart and soul to write our story – together, in partnership.
